q: Pressure, density and ____ are important quantities in physics and pressure is the basic of hydrostatic and hydrodynamic.
e: Pressure, density, and specific gravity are fundamental physical quantities, with pressure forming the basis of hydrostatics and hydrodynamics.

q: The study of fluids at rest is called ____ and the study of fluids at motion is hydrodynamic.
e: Hydrostatics is the branch of physics that studies fluids at rest, while hydrodynamics studies fluids in motion.

q: The study of fluids at rest is called hydrostatics and the study of fluids at motion is ____.
e: Hydrodynamics is the study of fluids in motion, contrasting with hydrostatics which studies fluids at rest.

q: Pressure is defined as the ____ exerted normally on unit area.
e: Pressure is the physical quantity representing the normal force applied per unit area of a surface.

q: Pressure is defined as the force exerted ____ on unit area.
e: The force in the pressure formula must act perpendicular (normally) to the surface area.

q: In SI units, pressure is measured in '____' (Pa).
e: The SI unit of pressure is the pascal, named after Blaise Pascal.

q: In SI units, pressure is measured in 'pascal' (____).
e: The symbol for the pascal, the SI unit of pressure, is Pa.

q: The force in the pressure formula must be normal (____) to the surface.
e: A normal force acts at a 90-degree angle perpendicular to the surface.

q: Pressure is a ____ quantity.
e: Pressure has magnitude but no specific direction, making it a scalar quantity.

q: From the definition of pressure, it is obtained that pointed nails penetrate the surfaces because for a definite force, the exerted ____ is too small.
e: A smaller contact area results in a higher pressure for the same applied force, allowing penetration.

q: Similarly sharp knives can cut easily than blunt knives because of smaller cutting ____.
e: A sharp knife has a very small cutting edge area, which increases the pressure exerted for a given force.

q: Elephants have four large flat feet so they reduce the ____ and less likely sink into the ground.
e: Large feet increase the contact area, thereby reducing the pressure exerted on the ground.

q: Most obvious is tractors used for ploughing has large tire areas so that they do not sink in the ____ fields.
e: Large tire areas distribute the tractor's weight over a larger surface, reducing pressure and preventing sinking in soft mud.

q: In FPS system, the unit of pressure is ____ (psi).
e: The FPS (Foot-Pound-Second) system uses pounds per square inch as the unit of pressure.

q: In Meteorology, the unit of pressure is ____ (hPa).
e: Meteorologists commonly use the hectopascal to measure atmospheric pressure.

q: Standard Atmospheric Pressure is ____ (1atm).
e: One atmosphere is defined as the standard atmospheric pressure at sea level.

q: $1 \text{ atm} = $ ____ $= 760 \text{ millimetre mercury (760 mm Hg)}$
e: One standard atmosphere is equivalent to 101,300 pascals or 760 mm of mercury.

q: $1 \text{ atm} = 1.013 \times 10^5 \text{ Pa} = $ ____
e: Standard atmospheric pressure can also be expressed as 760 millimetres of mercury.

q: $1 \text{ atm} = 1013 \text{ hPa} = $ ____
e: One atmosphere is equal to 1013 hectopascals, which is also equivalent to 1013 millibars.

q: $1 \text{ hPa} = $ ____ $= 1 \text{ mb}$
e: One hectopascal is equal to 100 pascals and is exactly equivalent to one millibar.
One pascal is a very small unit of pressure, equivalent to approximately 0.000145 psi.
One pound per square inch is equivalent to 6,900 pascals.

q: A person exerts pressure on the floor when standing, sitting and ____.
e: The pressure exerted by a person changes depending on their posture due to the varying contact area with the floor.

q: There is Myanmar riddle 'Which is heavier, a viss of cotton (or) a viss of ____ ?'
e: This riddle introduces the concept of density, as a viss of both has the same mass but different volumes.

q: Density is the ratio of ____ to volume of a substance.
e: Density is defined as the amount of mass per unit volume of a given substance.

q: Density is the ratio of mass to ____ of a substance.
e: Density is calculated by dividing the mass of a substance by its volume.

q: Density is the ____ quantity.
e: Density has magnitude but no direction, classifying it as a scalar quantity.

q: The Greek alphabet used to represent density is ____.
e: The Greek letter rho ($\rho$) is the standard symbol used to denote density in physics.

q: In SI unit, density is expressed in ____ ($\text{kg m}^{-3}$).
e: The standard SI unit for density is kilograms per cubic metre.

q: In SI unit, density is expressed in kilogram per cubic metre (____).
e: The symbol for the SI unit of density is kg m$^{-3}$.

q: In CGS unit, it is expressed in gram per cubic centimetre ($\text{g cm}^{-3}$) or gram per ____ ($\text{g mL}^{-1}$).
e: In the CGS system, density can also be expressed as grams per millilitre, which is equivalent to grams per cubic centimetre.

q: Mass of an object can be measured using a ____ and volume can be measured using a measuring cylinder.
e: A balance is the standard laboratory instrument used to measure the mass of an object.

q: Mass of an object can be measured using a balance and volume can be measured using a ____.
e: A measuring cylinder is commonly used to determine the volume of liquids or irregular solids via displacement.

q: Mass of the object does not change, but the ____ depends on the temperature.
e: While mass remains constant, the volume of a substance can expand or contract with changes in temperature.

q: If the volume changes, the ____ will change.
e: Since density is mass divided by volume, any change in volume (with constant mass) results in a change in density.

q: Average density of a human body is a little less than ____ density.
e: The human body's average density is slightly less than that of water, which is why humans can float.

q: The density of water at 4°C is ____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: Water reaches its maximum density of 1000 kg m$^{-3}$ at a temperature of 4°C.

q: The density of aluminium is ____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: Aluminium has a relatively low density of 2700 kg m$^{-3}$, making it useful for lightweight structures.

q: The density of copper is ____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: Copper is a dense metal with a density of 8900 kg m$^{-3}$.

q: The density of lead is ____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: Lead is a very dense metal, with a density of 11400 kg m$^{-3}$.

q: The density of mercury is ____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: Mercury is a liquid metal at room temperature with a high density of 13600 kg m$^{-3}$.

q: The density of gold is ____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: Gold is a very dense precious metal, with a density of 19300 kg m$^{-3}$.

q: The density of uranium is ____ $\text{kg m}^{-3}$.
e: Uranium is a heavy metal with a density of 19050 kg m$^{-3}$.

q: Relative density is how much a substance is denser than ____.
e: Relative density compares the density of a substance to the density of water at 4°C.

q: Relative density is also known as ____.
e: Specific gravity is an alternative term for relative density.

q: As the density of water is $1 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$ in CGS units, then density of substance can be taken as the ____.
e: In CGS units, the numerical value of a substance's density is equal to its relative density because water's density is 1.

q: As the relative density is the ratio of two densities, it is just a number without ____.
e: Because relative density is a ratio of two identical units, the units cancel out, leaving a dimensionless number.

q: Archimedes' Principle was formulated in ____.
e: Archimedes' Principle, a fundamental law of buoyancy, was discovered around 250 B.C.

q: When an object is partially (or) totally immersed in a liquid, the object displaces liquid volume that is equal to the volume of the ____ portion.
e: Archimedes' Principle Part I states that the displaced liquid volume equals the volume of the object that is submerged.

q: The loss in weight of the object is equal to the weight of the ____ displaced.
e: Archimedes' Principle Part II states that the apparent loss in weight equals the weight of the displaced fluid.

q: The upward thrust acting on a body which is immersed partially or totally in a liquid is equal to the ____ of the liquid displaced by the body.
e: The buoyant force (upward thrust) is exactly equal to the weight of the fluid that the body displaces.

q: upward thrust = uplift force = ____ = weight of liquid displaced
e: Upward thrust, uplift force, and buoyancy are synonymous terms describing the upward force exerted by a fluid.

q: By Archimedes' principle, weight of a body is more than buoyancy (or) upward thrust, it will ____ in the liquid.
e: If the gravitational force (weight) exceeds the upward buoyant force, the net force is downward, causing the object to sink.

q: Substances having relative density greater than ____ will sink in water.
e: A relative density greater than 1 means the substance is denser than water, causing it to sink.

q: King of ____ was suspicious with his crown; King let Archimedes to test whether the crown was made of pure gold.
e: The historical account of Archimedes testing the crown involves the King of Syracuse.

q: The crown had mass 3.75 kg or ____ g.
e: The mass of the King's crown was 3.75 kilograms, which is equivalent to 3750 grams.

q: As the density of gold is $19.3 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$, the crown must have volume ____ $\text{cm}^3$.
e: If the crown were pure gold, its volume would be calculated as mass divided by density, yielding 194 cm$^3$.

q: Archimedes found that the volume (by his principle Part I) was ____ $\text{cm}^3$.
e: Archimedes measured the actual volume of the crown by water displacement and found it to be 315 cm$^3$, proving it was not pure gold.

q: Then, he answered to the King that the crown was not ____.
e: The larger-than-expected volume indicated that a less dense metal had been mixed with the gold.

q: The added metal is ____ because it has similar color.
e: Copper is often used as an alloying metal with gold because it has a similar color but a lower density.

q: The student can extend the problem why the gold smith did not use ____ metal instead of copper.
e: Lead could have been used, but the problem prompts students to consider why copper was the more likely choice for deception.

q: The relative density of sulphur is ____.
e: Sulphur has a relative density of 2, meaning it is twice as dense as water.

q: When an object is placed in a liquid of a lower density, the object ____.
e: An object will sink if its density is greater than the density of the liquid it is placed in.

q: If it is placed in a liquid of a greater density, it ____.
e: An object will float if its density is less than the density of the surrounding liquid.

q: Since the amount of submerged portion for a floating body is inversely proportional to the specific gravity of the liquid, the more submerged, the ____ the specific gravity.
e: A floating object sinks deeper into liquids with lower specific gravity to displace enough weight to equal its own.

q: The hydrometer is an instrument for measuring the density (or) ____ of liquids.
e: A hydrometer is specifically designed to measure the density or relative density (specific gravity) of liquids.

q: It usually consists of a glass tube with a long ____ at one end.
e: The hydrometer's design features a long bulb at the bottom to provide buoyancy and stability.

q: The bulb is weighted with ____ so that the device floats vertically in the liquid.
e: Lead shot is added to the bulb to lower the center of gravity, ensuring the hydrometer floats upright.

q: If the hydrometer floats higher, it indicates that the liquid has a ____ density.
e: In a denser liquid, the hydrometer needs to displace less volume to equal its weight, so it floats higher.

q: The hydrometer sinks in the liquid until the weight of the liquid displaced is equal to the weight of the ____.
e: According to the law of flotation, a floating object displaces a weight of fluid equal to its own weight.

q: The hydrometer is calibrated to measure the density of the liquid in ____.
e: The stem of the hydrometer is marked with a scale calibrated in kilograms per cubic metre.

q: Special hydrometers are used to test the specific gravity of solutions in ____ in order to determine the condition of the battery.
e: Battery hydrometers measure the density of the electrolyte to determine the state of charge of a lead-acid battery.

q: The relative density of the acid in a fully charged car battery is ____.
e: A fully charged car battery typically has a sulfuric acid solution with a relative density of 1.25.

q: Milk and wine can be tested to make sure they have not been diluted with ____.
e: Hydrometers (like lactometers) are used in the food industry to detect adulteration by water, which lowers the density.

q: Hydrometer is a test tube like cylinder with overall density less than one (or) less than the density of ____.
e: To function properly, the overall density of the hydrometer must be less than that of the liquid it is designed to measure, typically water.

q: Weight of hydrometer = Weight of water displaced = (volume of water displaced × density of water) × ____.
e: The weight of the displaced fluid is calculated by multiplying its mass (volume × density) by the acceleration due to gravity (g).

q: An alloy is made by mixing 360 g of copper, of density $9 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$, with 80 g of ____, of density $8 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$.
e: This example illustrates how to calculate the density of an alloy by combining the masses and volumes of its constituent metals.

q: One litre of milk (density ____ $\text{g cm}^{-3}$) is mixed with 0.5 litre of water (density $1 \text{ g cm}^{-3}$).
e: This problem demonstrates calculating the density of a mixture using the known densities and volumes of the components.

q: Mini-submarine has the total volume of ____ $\text{m}^3$. Its mass is 2000 kg.
e: This example is used to determine if a submarine can carry additional load based on its volume and the density of water.

q: Normal atmospheric pressure 1 atm is equal to ____ Pa.
e: This conversion is frequently used in exercises to calculate the total force exerted by the atmosphere on a given surface area.
